To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) there is asymmetry between different types of base table modifications and (2) exploiting this asymmetry can lead to a substantial performance gain over traditional incremental view maintenance algorithms.

(i) the most efficient strategy for batch incremental view maintenance under a response time constraint is to selectively process batched modifications; (ii) this strategy is based on exploiting the natural asymmetries in the maintenance costs; and (iii) the strategy is effective even in the absence of perfect knowledge of future batch sizes.

(a) batch incremental maintenance is more efficient than incremental maintenance of individual modifications, (b) batch incremental maintenance can be further optimized by selectively processing modifications on some base table while batching others, and (c) our strategy is practical and can achieve significant savings over traditional approaches.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of efficient incremental view maintenance algorithms for a large class of applications.

the following question: How should we process batched modifications in order to maintain the view up to date within the given response time? We show that the answer is not always "as much as you can".

the following questions: How can we exploit asymmetries in incremental maintenance costs? How can we develop efficient algorithms to exploit these asymmetries? What are the performance benefits of such an exploitation?

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, in batch incremental view maintenance, it pays off to be asymmetric.
, in the presence of asymmetries, batch incremental view maintenance should not necessarily be performed in a uniform manner.
, in the context of view maintenance, the traditional "batch or nothing" approach should be replaced with an "asymmetric" approach that selectively processes batched modifications.

the performance of incremental view maintenance can be greatly improved by exploiting the asymmetry among base tables.
asymmetry is a powerful concept that can be used to develop more effective incremental view maintenance techniques.
